public_rationale: SimpleQA measures only short, fact-seeking questions with a single, verifiable answer (e1). An OpenAI and Harvard working paper looked at a representative sample of consumer ChatGPT conversations from May 2024 to June 2025. The post date falls inside that span (e2). In that study, the 'Seeking Information' topic was 14% of conversations in June 2024 and 24% in June 2025 (e2, e3). This category is broader than SimpleQA-style lookups. By mid-2025, Practical Guidance was about 29% and Writing was 24% (e2). The 'Asking' category was 49% of messages (e4). It is wider still and includes advice. Because the broader information-seeking category stayed well under half of usage in this period, SimpleQA-style lookups were not a majority of ChatGPT usage. That meets the contract's support condition.
limitations: The topic shares come from a news report on the working paper (e2, e3), because the full paper could not be fetched.
The study covers consumer plans only, not business or API use.
No source directly counts SimpleQA-style single-fact questions. The 'Seeking Information' share serves only as an upper bound.
The working paper is not peer-reviewed.

our_interpretation: What SimpleQA tests is short, fact-seeking questions with a single checkable answer.
Plain reading: short factual lookups of this kind are less than half of ChatGPT usage, measured by share of messages or conversations.

Target period: the year around the post, from mid-2024 to mid-2025. Zitron describes an ongoing state without naming a period. The only representative usage data covers this span, and the post falls inside it.
criteria.support_condition: Representative ChatGPT usage data from the target period shows that information-seeking, a category broader than SimpleQA-style lookups, is well under half of usage.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative usage data from the target period shows that short factual lookups make up a majority of ChatGPT messages or conversations.

evidence.excerpt: Practical Guidance remains around 29%. Writing declined from 36% to 24% over the past year. Seeking Information grew from 14% to 24%.
evidence.locator: section What People Use ChatGPT For
evidence.explanation: By mid-2025, information-seeking, a broader category than SimpleQA lookups, was about a quarter of usage, behind practical guidance and level with writing.

evidence.excerpt: “Seeking Information” messages now account for 24% of ChatGPT conversations, up from 14% a year earlier.
evidence.explanation: About nine months before the post, information-seeking was only 14% of conversations. Factual lookups were a small minority throughout the period.

evidence.excerpt: About half of messages (49%) are “Asking,” a growing and highly rated category
evidence.locator: section What they’re using it for, paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Even 'Asking', a wide category that includes advice as well as facts, is just under half of messages. Short factual lookups are therefore a smaller share still.
